title: Check Rock Mobile Content block processing context before relying on CurrentPerson
distilled_summary: Rock Mobile content can be rendered from bundled shell content or processed dynamically, and the available Lava context changes with those block settings. Before using `CurrentPerson`, secure lookups, page parameters, or database-backed personalization in a mobile Content block, verify Dynamic Content, Process Lava on Server, enabled Lava commands, and the intended context entity. If content is bundled into the shell download, do not assume the same authenticated server-side context or freshness that a dynamic server-rendered block would have.

title: Escape user, title, and URL text before inserting it into Rock Mobile XAML
distilled_summary: When Lava outputs XAML for Rock Mobile, escape any text that can contain content titles, user-entered strings, URLs, ampersands, quotes, apostrophes, or other markup-sensitive characters. Use the appropriate Lava escaping and URL encoding filters before putting values into XAML attributes or command/page parameters. Test with titles and names that contain punctuation so a single record cannot break the rendered mobile page or command parameter payload.

title: Treat anonymous SMS verification as a strict match plus server-side session recheck
distilled_summary: For anonymous forms that optionally verify a returning person by SMS, use strict matching before sending a code: name, email, mobile phone type, SMS-enabled phone, and birthdate rules should be explicit. Store verification state in a persisted workflow or equivalent server-side record with code hash, session token, expiration, attempt count, and verified flag. On final submit, re-check the verified server-side session before assigning a person alias or applicant context; do not trust only the browser state or a successful earlier step.

title: Avoid retaining plain SMS verification codes in communication history when not needed
distilled_summary: When a workflow sends a short-lived verification code, separate the operational code needed for delivery from the long-term audit state needed for verification. Store a hash, expiration, attempt count, and verified flag for server-side checking, and consider disabling or limiting communication history for the plain code message if the code should not remain visible after use. Verify the communication medium, sender, recipient person attribute, and retention behavior before enabling the flow broadly.

title: Guard connection-mutating actions when one signed-document workflow supports both pipeline and mass-send launches
distilled_summary: A signed-document workflow can often serve both connection-request launches and bulk audience launches, but connection-state actions must be guarded. Keep the signature, communication, and document steps independent of connection updates, and run connection-status or connection-request mutations only when the workflow actually has a ConnectionRequest context. This lets connection-driven launches continue normal pipeline behavior without letting mass-send launches accidentally change connection records.

title: Verify workflow attribute scope before adding defaults or repairing values
distilled_summary: Workflow attributes should be scoped to the intended WorkflowType through the correct entity type and qualifier. If an attribute with the same key exists without the expected qualifier, defaults or page-parameter writes can create misleading AttributeValue rows that appear in one UI surface but are invisible to SQL that reads the scoped workflow attribute. Before adding defaults, copying values, or repairing a workflow, check `EntityTypeId`, `EntityTypeQualifierColumn`, and `EntityTypeQualifierValue`; migrate only values that can be tied to the intended workflow type, and avoid bulk-moving default-value noise from unrelated workflows.

title: Use RawValue when copying a Single-Select workflow attribute that stores an internal ID
distilled_summary: A Single-Select workflow attribute can display a readable label while storing an internal value that later actions need, such as a DefinedValue ID, saved account ID, or other lookup key. When copying that stored value to another workflow attribute or using it in a validation query, use the raw attribute value rather than the formatted display output. Test with a label that differs from the stored ID and verify the downstream attribute contains the expected internal value before running dependent actions.

title: Validate saved payment account ownership, gateway, and type before workflow-triggered charges
distilled_summary: When a workflow charges a previously saved payment account, do not trust a selected saved-account ID by itself. Revalidate that the saved account belongs to the expected payer, belongs to the intended gateway, uses an eligible reusable payment type, and still exists immediately before charging. The authorization form may present a friendly label, but the payment action should operate on verified saved-account identity and should fail closed when the account is missing, revoked, wallet-only, or tied to a different payer or gateway.

title: Revalidate authorization and cancellation state immediately before delayed workflow payments
distilled_summary: A workflow Delay action is useful for scheduled follow-up charges or notices, but the world can change while the workflow is waiting. Before processing a delayed payment or other irreversible action, re-check the source workflow, authorization status, revocation state, saved-account eligibility, cancellation state, and any required audit metadata. Do not treat validation performed before the Delay as sufficient for the post-delay action, and make retries idempotent so a failed late step does not duplicate a charge or notification.

title: Re-sync local UI state after HTMX swaps replace rendered controls
distilled_summary: If a Rock CMS or Helix page stores UI state such as list/grid view, toggles, or expansion state in `sessionStorage` or `localStorage`, remember that an HTMX swap replaces the rendered controls. Re-apply state after `htmx:afterSwap`, or encode the state in URL parameters so the server can render the correct classes and ARIA state. Test the first render, swapped render, refresh, and back-button behavior; otherwise the data can be correct while the visible controls show stale state.
